findings.title: ensure_loaded! can crash or return early on nil @loaded_locales
findings.body: `ensure_loaded!` sets `@loaded_locales ||= []`, but `load_locale` returns early if the locale is already loaded and loads the `.rb` files only `if @loaded_locales.empty?`. Loading fallback locales first (e.g. :en before the current locale) is fine, but `translate` calls `@loaded_locales.include?` without initializing it. If `translate` runs before any `ensure_loaded!`, it raises NoMethodError on nil. Initialization should happen in one place, not only in the new method.

findings.title: Fallback list uses SiteSetting at lookup time and may fail when invoked early
findings.body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` calls `SiteSetting.default_locale` on every lookup. During boot, migrations or the asset precompile, the DB or settings may not be available, so any I18n lookup that consults fallbacks can raise. The `locale` argument can also be a string, which then fails to dedupe against the symbol `default_locale`, giving duplicate entries.

findings.title: Fallbacks included on I18n.backend.class at initializer time
findings.body: `I18n.backend.class` is included before the translate_accelerator patch is guaranteed to have run (relying on a file-ordering comment). It also silently depends on the backend being Simple. If the backend is later replaced, fallbacks are lost. The `config.i18n.fallbacks` removal also means the Rails-level setup is gone, so the behaviour is now enabled in every environment, including test and development, without a test.

findings.title: ensure_loaded! on every request
findings.body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` runs on each request and calls `SiteSetting.default_locale` and builds arrays each time. It is cheap after the first call, but the global `I18n.fallbacks` is only a custom Hash subclass. Anything that expects normal Hash behavior (such as `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` methods like `map`) will not work.
